text: Anuria: Anuria is nonpassage of urine, in practice is defined as passage of less than 100 milliliters of urine in a day. Anuria is often caused by failure in the function of kidneys.
Bladder pain: A presenting complaint characterised by bladder pain.
Cloudy urine: A presenting complaint characterised by cloudy urine.

Dribbling: In sports, dribbling is maneuvering a ball by one player while moving in a given direction, avoiding defenders' attempts to intercept the ball. A successful dribble will bring the ball past defenders legally and create opportunities to score.
Dysuria: Dysuria is a painful or otherwise uncomfortable sensation in the urethra associated with urination. It can be caused by various conditions, such as urinary tract infections.
Foamy urine: A presenting complaint characterised by foamy urine.

Frequency: Frequency is the number of occurrences of a repeating event per unit of time. Frequency is an important parameter used in science and engineering to specify the rate of oscillatory and vibratory phenomena, such as mechanical vibrations, audio signals (sound), radio waves, and light.

Haematuria: Hematuria or haematuria is defined as the presence of blood or red blood cells in the urine. "Gross hematuria" occurs when urine appears red, brown, or tea-colored due to the presence of blood.

Incomplete bladder emptying: Vesical tenesmus refers to the feeling of incomplete emptying of the bladder following urination. This sensation can be present even when the post-void residual urine volume is very small.

Nocturia: Nocturia is defined by the International Continence Society (ICS) as "the complaint that the individual has to wake at night one or more times for voiding ". The term is derived from Latin nox – "night", and Greek [τα] ούρα – "urine".

Oliguria: Oliguria or hypouresis is the low output of urine: specifically, more than 80 ml/day, but less than 400ml/day. The decreased output of urine may be a sign of dehydration, kidney failure, hypovolemic shock, hyperosmolar hyperglycemic nonketotic syndrome (HHNS), multiple organ dysfunction syndrome, urinary obstruction/urinary retention, diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), pre-eclampsia, and urinary tract infections, among other conditions.
Pneumaturia: Pneumaturia is the passage of gas or "air" in urine. This may be seen or described as "bubbles in the urine".
Polyuria: Polyuria is excessive or an abnormally large production or passage of urine. Increased production and passage of urine may also be termed as diuresis.
Poor urinary stream: A presenting complaint characterised by poor urinary stream.

Urgency: Urgency may refer to:Pan-pan, international radio calls for emergencies posing no imminent danger
Urinary urgency or Bowel urgency, medical symptoms
Urgency , 2007
Urgency , 2005
The Urgency, an album by Saving Grace.
Urinary hesitancy: Urinary retention is an inability to completely empty the bladder. Onset can be sudden or gradual.

Urinary incontinence: Urinary incontinence (UI), also known as involuntary urination, is any uncontrolled leakage of urine. It is a common and distressing problem, which may have a significant effect on quality of life.

Acute cystitis with hematuria: A urinary tract infection (UTI) is an infection that affects a part of the urinary tract, which includes the bladder, urethra and the kidney. Lower UTIs affect the bladder (cystitis) or urethra while upper UTIs affect the kidney (pyelonephritis). Common presenting complaints: Dysuria, Haematuria. Associated symptoms: Dysuria, Haematuria, Frequency, Urgency, Bladder Pain. Risk factors: Female Sex, Sexual Activity, Prior Urinary Tract Infection. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: female. Acute or chronic: acute.

Acute cystitis with hematuria red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_005) triggered by complaint 'DYSURIA': Dysuria with fever, rigors, flank pain — urosepsis/pyelonephritis. Red flag (RF_RU_013) triggered by complaint 'DYSURIA': Dysuria with discharge and sexual exposure — STI. Red flag (RF_RU_003) triggered by complaint 'HAEMATURIA': Haematuria with clots, flank pain, or fever. Red flag (RF_RU_004) triggered by complaint 'HAEMATURIA': Haematuria with weight loss or age >40.

Acute cystitis without hematuria: A urinary tract infection (UTI) is an infection that affects a part of the urinary tract, which includes the bladder, urethra and the kidney. Lower UTIs affect the bladder (cystitis) or urethra while upper UTIs affect the kidney (pyelonephritis). Common presenting complaints: Dysuria, Haematuria. Associated symptoms: Dysuria, Frequency, Urgency, Bladder Pain, Cloudy Urine. Risk factors: Female Sex, Sexual Activity, Prior Urinary Tract Infection, Diabetes Mellitus. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: female. Acute or chronic: acute.

Acute cystitis without hematuria red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_005) triggered by complaint 'DYSURIA': Dysuria with fever, rigors, flank pain — urosepsis/pyelonephritis. Red flag (RF_RU_013) triggered by complaint 'DYSURIA': Dysuria with discharge and sexual exposure — STI.

Acute cystitis without hematuria differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Acute Cystitis With Hematuria: Presence of visible haematuria on urinalysis is the sole distinguishing feature — same acute bacterial cystitis, different degree of mucosal involvement.

Amebic cystitis: A renal-urinary condition known as Amebic cystitis. Common presenting complaints: Dysuria. Associated symptoms: Dysuria, Haematuria, Frequency, Cloudy Urine, Bladder Pain. Risk factors: Travel To Endemic Area, Poor Sanitation Exposure, Immunosuppression. Age relevance: all_ages. Sex relevance: both. Acute or chronic: acute.

Amebic cystitis red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_005) triggered by complaint 'DYSURIA': Dysuria with fever, rigors, flank pain — urosepsis/pyelonephritis. Red flag (RF_RU_013) triggered by complaint 'DYSURIA': Dysuria with discharge and sexual exposure — STI.

Amebic cystitis differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Acute Cystitis Without Hematuria: Amebic cystitis is caused by Entamoeba histolytica, usually in a traveller or endemic-area resident; acute cystitis is bacterial (E. coli, Klebsiella) with no amebic exposure history.

Benign prostatic hyperplasia with lower urinary tract symptoms: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), also called prostate enlargement, is a noncancerous increase in size of the prostate gland. Symptoms may include frequent urination, trouble starting to urinate, weak stream, inability to urinate, or loss of bladder control. Common presenting complaints: Poor Urinary Stream, Nocturia, Urinary Hesitancy, Incomplete Bladder Emptying. Associated symptoms: Poor Urinary Stream, Urinary Hesitancy, Nocturia, Frequency, Incomplete Bladder Emptying, Dribbling. Risk factors: Older Male Age, Family History Bph, Obesity. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: male. Acute or chronic: chronic.

Benign prostatic hyperplasia with lower urinary tract symptoms red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_001) triggered by complaint 'POOR_URINARY_STREAM': BPH progressing to complete urinary retention. Red flag (RF_RU_010) triggered by complaint 'POOR_URINARY_STREAM': Poor stream with perineal pain and fever — prostate abscess.

Benign prostatic hyperplasia with lower urinary tract symptoms differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Unspecified Urethral Stricture Female: BPH occurs in males with prostate enlargement on DRE/ultrasound; urethral stricture (female) is a narrowing of the female urethra, confirmed on urethrogram or cystoscopy — different anatomy and sex.

Benign prostatic hyperplasia without lower urinary tract symptoms: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), also called prostate enlargement, is a noncancerous increase in size of the prostate gland. Symptoms may include frequent urination, trouble starting to urinate, weak stream, inability to urinate, or loss of bladder control. Common presenting complaints: Poor Urinary Stream. Associated symptoms: Typically Few Symptoms. Risk factors: Older Male Age, Family History Bph. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: male. Acute or chronic: chronic.

Benign prostatic hyperplasia without lower urinary tract symptoms red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_001) triggered by complaint 'POOR_URINARY_STREAM': BPH progressing to complete urinary retention. Red flag (RF_RU_010) triggered by complaint 'POOR_URINARY_STREAM': Poor stream with perineal pain and fever — prostate abscess.

Benign prostatic hyperplasia without lower urinary tract symptoms differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia With Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms: BPH with LUTS has documented lower urinary tract symptoms (poor stream, frequency, nocturia, hesitancy); BPH without LUTS is an incidental finding on exam/imaging with no symptomatic urinary complaints yet.

Candidal cystitis and urethritis: A renal-urinary condition known as Candidal cystitis and urethritis. Common presenting complaints: Dysuria. Associated symptoms: Dysuria, Frequency, Cloudy Urine, Bladder Pain. Risk factors: Recent Antibiotic Use, Immunosuppression, Diabetes Mellitus, Indwelling Urinary Catheter. Age relevance: all_ages. Sex relevance: both. Acute or chronic: both.

Candidal cystitis and urethritis red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_005) triggered by complaint 'DYSURIA': Dysuria with fever, rigors, flank pain — urosepsis/pyelonephritis. Red flag (RF_RU_013) triggered by complaint 'DYSURIA': Dysuria with discharge and sexual exposure — STI.

Candidal cystitis and urethritis differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Acute Cystitis Without Hematuria: Candidal infection is fungal (Candida species), usually in an immunocompromised or antibiotic-exposed patient; acute bacterial cystitis is bacterial, confirmed by urine culture with bacterial growth.

Chlamydial cystitis and urethritis: A renal-urinary condition known as Chlamydial cystitis and urethritis. Common presenting complaints: Dysuria. Associated symptoms: Dysuria, Urethral Discharge, Frequency, Cloudy Urine. Risk factors: Unprotected Sexual Intercourse, Multiple Sexual Partners, Young Adult Age. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: both. Acute or chronic: acute.

Chlamydial cystitis and urethritis red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_005) triggered by complaint 'DYSURIA': Dysuria with fever, rigors, flank pain — urosepsis/pyelonephritis. Red flag (RF_RU_013) triggered by complaint 'DYSURIA': Dysuria with discharge and sexual exposure — STI.

Chlamydial cystitis and urethritis differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Acute Cystitis Without Hematuria: Chlamydial infection is an STI (Chlamydia trachomatis), often with urethral discharge and sexual exposure history; acute cystitis is non-sexually-transmitted bacterial infection, confirmed by standard urine culture.

Congenital renal failure: A renal-urinary condition known as Congenital renal failure. Common presenting complaints: Oliguria. Associated symptoms: Leg Swelling, Feeling Tired, Reduced Urination, Foamy Urine, Loss Of Appetite, Confusion. Risk factors: Congenital Urinary Tract Anomaly, Genetic Syndrome, Maternal Drug Exposure. Age relevance: neonatal. Sex relevance: both. Acute or chronic: chronic.
Congenital renal failure red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_012) triggered by complaint 'OLIGURIA': Oliguria/anuria with confusion or severe oedema — acute kidney injury.

Congenital renal failure differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Hypertensive Heart And Chronic Kidney Disease Without Heart Failure With Stage 5 Chronic Kidney Disease Or End Stage Renal Disease: Congenital renal failure is present from birth (neonatal/infant presentation, congenital anomalies of kidney); hypertensive CKD develops progressively in adults with chronic hypertension.

Diabetes insipidus: Diabetes insipidus (DI) is a condition characterized by large amounts of dilute urine and increased thirst. The amount of urine produced can be nearly 20 liters per day. Common presenting complaints: Polyuria. Associated symptoms: Polyuria, Polydipsia, Nocturia, Dehydration, Feeling Tired. Risk factors: Brain Tumour Or Surgery, Head Injury, Inflammatory Disease Hypothalamus. Age relevance: all_ages. Sex relevance: both. Acute or chronic: chronic.

Diabetes insipidus differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus: Central diabetes insipidus is caused by insufficient ADH secretion from the hypothalamus/pituitary and responds to desmopressin; nephrogenic DI is caused by renal resistance to ADH and does NOT respond to desmopressin — the water deprivation test distinguishes them.

Diphtheritic cystitis: A renal-urinary condition known as Diphtheritic cystitis. Common presenting complaints: Dysuria. Associated symptoms: Dysuria, Haematuria, Fever, Cloudy Urine, Bladder Pain. Risk factors: Unvaccinated For Diphtheria, Travel To Endemic Area, Pediatric Age. Age relevance: pediatric. Sex relevance: both. Acute or chronic: acute.

Diphtheritic cystitis red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_005) triggered by complaint 'DYSURIA': Dysuria with fever, rigors, flank pain — urosepsis/pyelonephritis. Red flag (RF_RU_013) triggered by complaint 'DYSURIA': Dysuria with discharge and sexual exposure — STI.

Diphtheritic cystitis differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Acute Cystitis Without Hematuria: Diphtheritic cystitis is caused by Corynebacterium diphtheriae and forms a pseudomembrane on the bladder mucosa; acute cystitis is a common bacterial UTI without pseudomembrane formation.

Gestational proteinuria, complicating childbirth: A renal-urinary condition known as Gestational proteinuria, complicating childbirth. Common presenting complaints: Foamy Urine. Associated symptoms: Typically Few Symptoms, Foamy Urine. Risk factors: Pre Existing Hypertension, Pre Existing Renal Disease. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: female. Acute or chronic: acute.

Gestational proteinuria, complicating childbirth red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_011) triggered by complaint 'FOAMY_URINE': Foamy urine in pregnancy with headache or hypertension — pre-eclampsia. Red flag (RF_RU_007) triggered by complaint 'FOAMY_URINE': Foamy urine with progressive oedema — nephrotic syndrome.

Gestational proteinuria, complicating childbirth differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Gestational Proteinuria Complicating The Puerperium: Complicating childbirth is during active delivery; complicating the puerperium is the postnatal period (up to 6 weeks after delivery) — same gestational proteinuria, different timing.

Gestational proteinuria, complicating the puerperium: A renal-urinary condition known as Gestational proteinuria, complicating the puerperium. Common presenting complaints: Foamy Urine. Associated symptoms: Typically Few Symptoms, Foamy Urine. Risk factors: Pre Existing Hypertension, Pre Existing Renal Disease. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: female. Acute or chronic: acute.

Gestational proteinuria, complicating the puerperium red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_011) triggered by complaint 'FOAMY_URINE': Foamy urine in pregnancy with headache or hypertension — pre-eclampsia. Red flag (RF_RU_007) triggered by complaint 'FOAMY_URINE': Foamy urine with progressive oedema — nephrotic syndrome.

Gestational proteinuria, first trimester: A renal-urinary condition known as Gestational proteinuria, first trimester. Common presenting complaints: Foamy Urine. Associated symptoms: Foamy Urine, Typically Few Symptoms. Risk factors: Pre Existing Renal Disease. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: female. Acute or chronic: acute.

Gestational proteinuria, first trimester red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_011) triggered by complaint 'FOAMY_URINE': Foamy urine in pregnancy with headache or hypertension — pre-eclampsia. Red flag (RF_RU_007) triggered by complaint 'FOAMY_URINE': Foamy urine with progressive oedema — nephrotic syndrome.

Gestational proteinuria, first trimester differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Gestational Proteinuria Second Trimester: Defined purely by gestational timing: first trimester is <13 weeks, second trimester is 13–26 weeks — same clinical entity, different gestational stage.

Gestational proteinuria, second trimester: A renal-urinary condition known as Gestational proteinuria, second trimester. Common presenting complaints: Foamy Urine. Associated symptoms: Foamy Urine, Typically Few Symptoms. Risk factors: Pre Existing Renal Disease. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: female. Acute or chronic: acute.

Gestational proteinuria, second trimester red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_011) triggered by complaint 'FOAMY_URINE': Foamy urine in pregnancy with headache or hypertension — pre-eclampsia. Red flag (RF_RU_007) triggered by complaint 'FOAMY_URINE': Foamy urine with progressive oedema — nephrotic syndrome.

Gestational proteinuria, third trimester: A renal-urinary condition known as Gestational proteinuria, third trimester. Common presenting complaints: Foamy Urine. Associated symptoms: Typically Few Symptoms, Foamy Urine, Leg Swelling. Risk factors: Pre Existing Hypertension, Pre Existing Renal Disease. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: female. Acute or chronic: acute.

Gestational proteinuria, third trimester red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_011) triggered by complaint 'FOAMY_URINE': Foamy urine in pregnancy with headache or hypertension — pre-eclampsia. Red flag (RF_RU_007) triggered by complaint 'FOAMY_URINE': Foamy urine with progressive oedema — nephrotic syndrome.

Gestational proteinuria, third trimester differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Gestational Proteinuria Complicating Childbirth: Third trimester is during the antenatal period (>26 weeks, pre-delivery); complicating childbirth is diagnosed during the active labour and delivery event.

Gestational proteinuria, unspecified trimester: A renal-urinary condition known as Gestational proteinuria, unspecified trimester. Common presenting complaints: Foamy Urine. Associated symptoms: Foamy Urine, Leg Swelling, Typically Few Symptoms. Risk factors: Pre Existing Hypertension, Pre Existing Renal Disease. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: female. Acute or chronic: acute.

Gestational proteinuria, unspecified trimester red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_011) triggered by complaint 'FOAMY_URINE': Foamy urine in pregnancy with headache or hypertension — pre-eclampsia. Red flag (RF_RU_007) triggered by complaint 'FOAMY_URINE': Foamy urine with progressive oedema — nephrotic syndrome.

Gestational proteinuria, unspecified trimester differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Gestational Proteinuria First Trimester: Unspecified trimester is used when the gestational age at diagnosis is not documented; first trimester is used when gestational age is confirmed as <13 weeks.

Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease with heart failure and with stage 5 chronic kidney disease, or end stage renal disease: A renal-urinary condition known as Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease with heart failure and with stage 5 chronic kidney disease, or end stage renal disease. Common presenting complaints: Oliguria. Associated symptoms: Reduced Urination, Leg Swelling, Shortness Of Breath, Foamy Urine, Nocturia. Risk factors: Chronic Hypertension, Diabetes Mellitus, Coronary Artery Disease. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: both. Acute or chronic: chronic.

Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease with heart failure and with stage 5 chronic kidney disease, or end stage renal disease red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_012) triggered by complaint 'OLIGURIA': Oliguria/anuria with confusion or severe oedema — acute kidney injury.

Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease without heart failure, with stage 5 chronic kidney disease, or end stage renal disease: A renal-urinary condition known as Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease without heart failure, with stage 5 chronic kidney disease, or end stage renal disease. Common presenting complaints: Oliguria. Associated symptoms: Reduced Urination, Leg Swelling, Foamy Urine, Feeling Tired, Nocturia. Risk factors: Chronic Hypertension, Diabetes Mellitus, Older Age. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: both. Acute or chronic: chronic.

Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease without heart failure, with stage 5 chronic kidney disease, or end stage renal disease red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_012) triggered by complaint 'OLIGURIA': Oliguria/anuria with confusion or severe oedema — acute kidney injury.

Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease without heart failure, with stage 5 chronic kidney disease, or end stage renal disease differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Hypertensive Heart And Chronic Kidney Disease With Heart Failure And With Stage 5 Chronic Kidney Disease Or End Stage Renal Disease: Both are hypertensive CKD at stage 5/ESRD; the 'with heart failure' variant has concurrent clinical heart failure (dyspnoea, reduced EF on echo) in addition to the renal disease.

Hypertensive urgency: A hypertensive urgency is a clinical situation in which blood pressure is very high with minimal or no symptoms, and no signs or symptoms indicating acute organ damage. This contrasts with a hypertensive emergency where severely high blood pressure is accompanied by evidence of progressive organ or system damage. Common presenting complaints: Urgency. Associated symptoms: Headache, Shortness Of Breath, Chest Pain, Nausea, Blurred Vision. Risk factors: Chronic Hypertension, Non Compliance Antihypertensive, Chronic Kidney Disease. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: both. Acute or chronic: acute.
Hypertensive urgency red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_006) triggered by complaint 'URGENCY': Urgency with BP ≥180/120 and headache/visual change/confusion.

Interstitial cystitis (chronic) with hematuria: Interstitial cystitis (IC) or bladder pain syndrome (BPS), is chronic pain in the bladder and pelvic floor of unknown cause. Symptoms include feeling the need to urinate right away, needing to urinate often, bladder pain and pain with sex. Common presenting complaints: Bladder Pain. Associated symptoms: Bladder Pain, Haematuria, Frequency, Urgency, Nocturia. Risk factors: Female Sex, Autoimmune Disorder. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: female. Acute or chronic: chronic.

Interstitial cystitis (chronic) with hematuria red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_005) triggered by complaint 'BLADDER_PAIN': Bladder pain with fever — rule out superimposed infection. Red flag (RF_RU_014) triggered by complaint 'BLADDER_PAIN': Interstitial cystitis with gross haematuria.

Interstitial cystitis (chronic) with hematuria differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Trigonitis With Hematuria: Interstitial cystitis affects the whole bladder wall with Hunner lesions on cystoscopy; trigonitis is localised inflammation of the bladder trigone only, seen as epithelial changes at the trigone on cystoscopy.

Interstitial cystitis (chronic) without hematuria: Interstitial cystitis (IC) or bladder pain syndrome (BPS), is chronic pain in the bladder and pelvic floor of unknown cause. Symptoms include feeling the need to urinate right away, needing to urinate often, bladder pain and pain with sex. Common presenting complaints: Bladder Pain. Associated symptoms: Bladder Pain, Frequency, Urgency, Dysuria, Nocturia. Risk factors: Female Sex, Autoimmune Disorder, Prior Pelvic Surgery. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: female. Acute or chronic: chronic.
Interstitial cystitis (chronic) without hematuria red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_005) triggered by complaint 'BLADDER_PAIN': Bladder pain with fever — rule out superimposed infection.

Interstitial cystitis (chronic) without hematuria differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Interstitial Cystitis Chronic With Hematuria: Presence of haematuria on urinalysis distinguishes these — same chronic interstitial cystitis, IC with hematuria has mucosal bleeding seen on cystoscopy (Hunner lesions more likely). Compared to Acute Cystitis Without Hematuria: Interstitial cystitis is chronic (>6 weeks), culture-negative, and does not respond to antibiotics; acute cystitis is short-duration, culture-positive, and antibiotic-responsive.

Irradiation cystitis with hematuria: A renal-urinary condition known as Irradiation cystitis with hematuria. Common presenting complaints: Haematuria. Associated symptoms: Haematuria, Dysuria, Frequency, Bladder Pain, Urgency. Risk factors: Pelvic Radiotherapy, Bladder Cancer Treatment. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: both. Acute or chronic: chronic.

Irradiation cystitis with hematuria red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_003) triggered by complaint 'HAEMATURIA': Haematuria with clots, flank pain, or fever. Red flag (RF_RU_004) triggered by complaint 'HAEMATURIA': Haematuria with weight loss or age >40.

Irradiation cystitis with hematuria differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Other Cystitis With Hematuria: Irradiation cystitis has a clear history of pelvic radiotherapy; other cystitis with haematuria has no radiation history and may represent chemical, viral, or idiopathic causes.

Irradiation cystitis without hematuria: A renal-urinary condition known as Irradiation cystitis without hematuria. Common presenting complaints: Dysuria, Haematuria. Associated symptoms: Dysuria, Frequency, Urgency, Bladder Pain. Risk factors: Pelvic Radiotherapy, Bladder Cancer Treatment. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: both. Acute or chronic: both.
Irradiation cystitis without hematuria red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_003) triggered by complaint 'HAEMATURIA': Irradiation cystitis developing haematuria with clots.

Irradiation cystitis without hematuria differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Acute Cystitis Without Hematuria: Irradiation cystitis follows a history of pelvic radiotherapy; acute cystitis has no radiation exposure history and responds to antibiotics, which irradiation cystitis does not. Compared to Irradiation Cystitis With Hematuria: Same radiation-induced bladder injury; haematuria is present in the 'with haematuria' variant, indicating more severe mucosal damage or telangiectasia formation.

Irritant contact dermatitis due to fecal, urinary or dual incontinence: Irritant contact dermatitis is a form of contact dermatitis that can be divided into forms caused by chemical irritants and those caused by physical irritants. Common presenting complaints: Urinary Incontinence. Associated symptoms: Skin Redness Groin, Skin Pain Groin, Urinary Incontinence, Skin Breakdown Groin. Risk factors: Urinary Incontinence, Faecal Incontinence, Immobility. Age relevance: all_ages. Sex relevance: both. Acute or chronic: both.
Irritant contact dermatitis due to fecal, urinary or dual incontinence red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_009) triggered by complaint 'URINARY_INCONTINENCE': New incontinence after trauma or spinal injury.

Isolated proteinuria with minor glomerular abnormality: Proteinuria is the presence of excess proteins in the urine. In healthy persons, urine contains very little protein, less than 150 mg/day; an excess is suggestive of illness. Common presenting complaints: Foamy Urine. Associated symptoms: Foamy Urine, Typically Few Symptoms, Leg Swelling. Risk factors: Diabetes Mellitus, Chronic Hypertension. Age relevance: all_ages. Sex relevance: both. Acute or chronic: chronic.
Isolated proteinuria with minor glomerular abnormality red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_007) triggered by complaint 'FOAMY_URINE': Foamy urine with leg/facial oedema — nephrotic range proteinuria.

Isolated proteinuria with minor glomerular abnormality differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Gestational Proteinuria Unspecified Trimester: Isolated proteinuria with glomerular abnormality is a non-pregnancy glomerular disease; gestational proteinuria is specifically pregnancy-related and resolves postpartum.

Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus: Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (NDI), also known as arginine vasopressin resistance (AVP-R) and previously known as renal diabetes insipidus, is a form of diabetes insipidus primarily due to pathology of the kidney. This is in contrast to central or neurogenic diabetes insipidus, which is caused by insufficient levels of vasopressin. Common presenting complaints: Polyuria. Associated symptoms: Polyuria, Nocturia, Polydipsia, Dehydration, Feeling Tired. Risk factors: Lithium Therapy, Chronic Kidney Disease, Hypercalcaemia, Genetic Mutation Avpr2. Age relevance: all_ages. Sex relevance: both. Acute or chronic: chronic.

Other cystitis with hematuria: A urinary tract infection (UTI) is an infection that affects a part of the urinary tract, which includes the bladder, urethra and the kidney. Lower UTIs affect the bladder (cystitis) or urethra while upper UTIs affect the kidney (pyelonephritis). Common presenting complaints: Haematuria. Associated symptoms: Haematuria, Dysuria, Frequency, Bladder Pain. Risk factors: Immunosuppression, Chemical Exposure Bladder. Age relevance: all_ages. Sex relevance: both. Acute or chronic: both.

Other cystitis with hematuria red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_003) triggered by complaint 'HAEMATURIA': Haematuria with clots, flank pain, or fever. Red flag (RF_RU_004) triggered by complaint 'HAEMATURIA': Haematuria with weight loss or age >40.

Other cystitis without hematuria: A urinary tract infection (UTI) is an infection that affects a part of the urinary tract, which includes the bladder, urethra and the kidney. Lower UTIs affect the bladder (cystitis) or urethra while upper UTIs affect the kidney (pyelonephritis). Common presenting complaints: Haematuria. Associated symptoms: Dysuria, Frequency, Bladder Pain, Cloudy Urine. Risk factors: Immunosuppression, Chemical Exposure Bladder. Age relevance: all_ages. Sex relevance: both. Acute or chronic: both.

Other cystitis without hematuria differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Other Cystitis With Hematuria: Presence of haematuria distinguishes these two — same non-specific cystitis of unspecified cause. Compared to Interstitial Cystitis Chronic Without Hematuria: Other cystitis is a short-term or unspecified condition without confirmed interstitial pathology; interstitial cystitis is a chronic (>6 week) diagnosis of exclusion with characteristic cystoscopy findings.

Other specified urinary incontinence: Urinary incontinence (UI), also known as involuntary urination, is any uncontrolled leakage of urine. It is a common and distressing problem, which may have a significant effect on quality of life. Common presenting complaints: Urinary Incontinence. Associated symptoms: Urinary Incontinence, Frequency. Risk factors: Neurological Disorder, Older Age. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: both. Acute or chronic: chronic.
Other specified urinary incontinence red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_009) triggered by complaint 'URINARY_INCONTINENCE': New incontinence after trauma or spinal injury.

Other specified urinary incontinence differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Irritant Contact Dermatitis Due To Fecal Urinary Or Dual Incontinence: Other specified incontinence is the underlying leakage disorder; irritant dermatitis is the downstream skin consequence of ongoing leakage.

Other urethral stricture, female: A urethral stricture is a narrowing of the urethra, the tube connected to the bladder that allows urination. The narrowing reduces the flow of urine and makes it more difficult or even painful to empty the bladder. Common presenting complaints: Poor Urinary Stream. Associated symptoms: Poor Urinary Stream, Urinary Hesitancy, Dysuria, Incomplete Bladder Emptying. Risk factors: Prior Urological Procedure, Recurrent Uti. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: female. Acute or chronic: chronic.
Other urethral stricture, female red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_001) triggered by complaint 'POOR_URINARY_STREAM': Urethral stricture causing complete urinary retention.

Other urethral stricture, female differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Unspecified Urethral Stricture Female: Other urethral stricture (female) has an identifiable but non-postprocedural/non-traumatic cause; unspecified has no documented aetiology.

Overactive bladder: Overactive bladder (OAB) is a common condition where there is a frequent feeling of needing to urinate to a degree that it negatively affects a person's life. Overactive bladder is characterized by a group of four symptoms: urgency, urinary frequency, nocturia, and urge incontinence. Common presenting complaints: Frequency. Associated symptoms: Urgency, Frequency, Nocturia, Urinary Incontinence. Risk factors: Older Age, Neurological Disorder, Female Sex, Obesity. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: both. Acute or chronic: chronic.

Overactive bladder differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Hypertensive Urgency: Overactive bladder is a urological syndrome with urinary urgency/frequency driven by detrusor overactivity; hypertensive urgency is a cardiovascular emergency driven by severely elevated blood pressure — the word 'urgency' is unrelated. Compared to Interstitial Cystitis Chronic Without Hematuria: Overactive bladder has urgency with frequency but no bladder pain; interstitial cystitis has chronic bladder/pelvic pain as the dominant symptom with urgency secondary to pain rather than detrusor overactivity.

Post-traumatic anterior urethral stricture: A renal-urinary condition known as Post-traumatic anterior urethral stricture. Common presenting complaints: Poor Urinary Stream. Associated symptoms: Poor Urinary Stream, Urinary Hesitancy, Dribbling, Incomplete Bladder Emptying. Risk factors: Pelvic Trauma, Straddle Injury. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: male. Post-traumatic bulbous urethral stricture red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_001) triggered by complaint 'POOR_URINARY_STREAM': Urethral stricture causing complete urinary retention.

Post-traumatic bulbous urethral stricture differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Post Traumatic Membranous Urethral Stricture: Post-traumatic bulbous urethral stricture involves the bulbar urethra (commonest site for straddle injury); membranous urethral stricture involves the membranous urethra (typically from pelvic fracture injury to the posterior urethra).

Post-traumatic membranous urethral stricture: A renal-urinary condition known as Post-traumatic membranous urethral stricture. Common presenting complaints: Poor Urinary Stream. Associated symptoms: Poor Urinary Stream, Urinary Hesitancy, Incomplete Bladder Emptying, Haematuria. Risk factors: Pelvic Fracture, Pelvic Trauma. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: male. Post-traumatic membranous urethral stricture red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_001) triggered by complaint 'POOR_URINARY_STREAM': Urethral stricture causing complete urinary retention.

Post-traumatic membranous urethral stricture differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Post Traumatic Anterior Urethral Stricture: Membranous stricture is in the posterior urethra (pelvic fracture mechanism); anterior urethral stricture covers both bulbar and penile urethra strictures from straddle or instrumentation injury.

Post-void dribbling: Post-void dribbling, also known as post-micturition dribbling (PMD), occurs when urine remaining in the urethra after voiding the bladder dribbles out after urination has completed. A common and usually benign complaint, it may be a symptom of urethral diverticulum, prostatitis and other medical problems. Common presenting complaints: Dribbling. Associated symptoms: Dribbling, Incomplete Bladder Emptying, Poor Urinary Stream. Risk factors: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia, Urethral Stricture, Pelvic Floor Weakness. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: both. Acute or chronic: chronic.
Post-void dribbling red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_010) triggered by complaint 'DRIBBLING': Post-void dribbling with perineal pain and fever.

Post-void dribbling differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia With Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms: Post-void dribbling occurs specifically after micturition ends due to residual urine in the bulbar urethra; BPH with LUTS causes poor stream and hesitancy throughout voiding, not just at the end. Compared to Post Traumatic Bulbous Urethral Stricture: Post-void dribbling is a functional pooling of urine in the bulbar urethra without a fixed structural narrowing; post-traumatic bulbous stricture is a fixed narrowing confirmed on urethrogram — both can coexist after perineal trauma.

Postprocedural urethral stricture, female: A renal-urinary condition known as Postprocedural urethral stricture, female. Common presenting complaints: Poor Urinary Stream. Associated symptoms: Poor Urinary Stream, Urinary Hesitancy, Incomplete Bladder Emptying, Dysuria. Risk factors: Urethral Catheterisation, Prior Urological Surgery. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: female. Acute or chronic: chronic.
Postprocedural urethral stricture, female red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_001) triggered by complaint 'POOR_URINARY_STREAM': Urethral stricture causing complete urinary retention.

Postprocedural urethral stricture, female differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Other Urethral Stricture Female: Postprocedural stricture follows a documented urological procedure (catheterisation, surgery); other urethral stricture (female) has no identified postprocedural cause.

Postural (urinary) incontinence: A renal-urinary condition known as Postural (urinary) incontinence. Common presenting complaints: Urinary Incontinence. Associated symptoms: Urinary Incontinence, Frequency, Urgency. Risk factors: Female Sex, Pelvic Floor Weakness, Prior Childbirth. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: female. Acute or chronic: chronic.
Postural (urinary) incontinence red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_009) triggered by complaint 'URINARY_INCONTINENCE': New incontinence after trauma or spinal injury.

Postural (urinary) incontinence differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Other Specified Urinary Incontinence: Postural incontinence leaks specifically on change of body position; other specified incontinence covers mixed or atypical patterns that do not fit standard stress/urge/postural categories. Compared to Irritant Contact Dermatitis Due To Fecal Urinary Or Dual Incontinence: Postural incontinence is the primary urological leakage disorder; irritant dermatitis is a secondary skin complication from prolonged urine contact — both can coexist but the dermatitis is not the urinary diagnosis.

Primary membranous nephropathy with isolated proteinuria: A renal-urinary condition known as Primary membranous nephropathy with isolated proteinuria. Common presenting complaints: Foamy Urine. Associated symptoms: Foamy Urine, Leg Swelling, Typically Few Symptoms, Feeling Tired. Risk factors: Autoimmune Disorder, Hepatitis B Infection, Nsaid Use. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: both. Acute or chronic: chronic.
Primary membranous nephropathy with isolated proteinuria red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_007) triggered by complaint 'FOAMY_URINE': Foamy urine with leg/facial oedema — nephrotic range proteinuria.

Primary membranous nephropathy with isolated proteinuria differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Isolated Proteinuria With Minor Glomerular Abnormality: Primary membranous nephropathy has characteristic sub-epithelial immune deposits on renal biopsy (PLA2R antibody positive); isolated proteinuria with minor glomerular abnormality has minimal biopsy changes without membranous pattern.

Renal failure following complete or unspecified spontaneous abortion: Kidney failure, also known as renal failure or end-stage renal disease (ESRD), is a medical condition in which the kidneys can no longer adequately filter waste products from the blood, functioning at less than 15% of normal levels. Kidney failure is classified as either acute kidney failure, which develops rapidly and may resolve; and chronic kidney failure, which develops slowly and can often be irreversible. Common presenting complaints: Oliguria. Associated symptoms: Reduced Urination, Leg Swelling, Feeling Tired, Foamy Urine. Risk factors: Sepsis Or Hemorrhage During Procedure, Prior Renal Disease. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: female. Acute or chronic: acute.

Renal failure following complete or unspecified spontaneous abortion red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_012) triggered by complaint 'OLIGURIA': Oliguria/anuria with confusion or severe oedema — acute kidney injury. Red flag (RF_RU_011) triggered by complaint 'OLIGURIA': Oliguria in pregnancy context — rule out pre-eclampsia.

Traumatic anuria, initial encounter differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Traumatic Anuria Subsequent Encounter: Initial encounter is the first active treatment visit after trauma; subsequent encounter is any follow-up visit for the same injury event.

Traumatic anuria, sequela red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_002) triggered by complaint 'ANURIA': No urine output following trauma. Red flag (RF_RU_001) triggered by complaint 'ANURIA': Complete inability to pass urine.

Traumatic anuria, subsequent encounter red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_002) triggered by complaint 'ANURIA': No urine output following trauma. Red flag (RF_RU_001) triggered by complaint 'ANURIA': Complete inability to pass urine.

Traumatic anuria, subsequent encounter differential diagnosis notes. Trichomonal cystitis and urethritis: A renal-urinary condition known as Trichomonal cystitis and urethritis. Common presenting complaints: Dysuria. Associated symptoms: Dysuria, Vaginal Discharge, Frequency, Cloudy Urine, Bladder Pain. Risk factors: Unprotected Sexual Intercourse, Multiple Sexual Partners, Female Sex. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: female. Acute or chronic: acute.

Trichomonal cystitis and urethritis red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_005) triggered by complaint 'DYSURIA': Dysuria with fever, rigors, flank pain — urosepsis/pyelonephritis. Red flag (RF_RU_013) triggered by complaint 'DYSURIA': Dysuria with discharge and sexual exposure — STI.

Trichomonal cystitis and urethritis differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Chlamydial Cystitis And Urethritis: Trichomonal infection is caused by Trichomonas vaginalis (often with frothy vaginal discharge); chlamydial infection is caused by Chlamydia trachomatis (often with mucopurulent discharge) — differentiated by STI swab.

Trigonitis with hematuria: Trigonitis is a condition of inflammation of the trigone region of the bladder. It is more common in women. Common presenting complaints: Haematuria. Associated symptoms: Haematuria, Bladder Pain, Frequency, Urgency, Dysuria. Risk factors: Female Sex, Recurrent Uti. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: both. Acute or chronic: chronic.

Trigonitis with hematuria red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_003) triggered by complaint 'HAEMATURIA': Haematuria with clots, flank pain, or fever. Red flag (RF_RU_004) triggered by complaint 'HAEMATURIA': Haematuria with weight loss or age >40.

Trigonitis with hematuria differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Acute Cystitis With Hematuria: Trigonitis is localised to the trigone (confirmed on cystoscopy); acute cystitis involves diffuse bladder mucosal inflammation with positive urine culture.

Trigonitis without hematuria: Trigonitis is a condition of inflammation of the trigone region of the bladder. It is more common in women. Common presenting complaints: Haematuria. Associated symptoms: Bladder Pain, Frequency, Urgency, Dysuria. Risk factors: Female Sex, Recurrent Uti. Age relevance: all_ages. Sex relevance: female. Acute or chronic: chronic.

Trigonitis without hematuria differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Trigonitis With Hematuria: Presence of haematuria on urinalysis is the only distinguishing feature — same inflammation of the bladder trigone, different degree of mucosal bleeding.

Unspecified urethral stricture, female: A urethral stricture is a narrowing of the urethra, the tube connected to the bladder that allows urination. The narrowing reduces the flow of urine and makes it more difficult or even painful to empty the bladder. Common presenting complaints: Poor Urinary Stream. Associated symptoms: Poor Urinary Stream, Urinary Hesitancy, Dysuria. Risk factors: Prior Urological Procedure. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: female. Acute or chronic: chronic.
Unspecified urethral stricture, female red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_001) triggered by complaint 'POOR_URINARY_STREAM': Urethral stricture causing complete urinary retention.

Vesical fistula, not elsewhere classified: A renal-urinary condition known as Vesical fistula, not elsewhere classified. Common presenting complaints: Pneumaturia. Associated symptoms: Pneumaturia, Cloudy Urine, Recurrent Uti, Haematuria, Dysuria. Risk factors: Prior Pelvic Surgery, Pelvic Radiotherapy, Inflammatory Bowel Disease. Age relevance: adult. Sex relevance: both. Acute or chronic: chronic.
Vesical fistula, not elsewhere classified red flags. Red flag (RF_RU_008) triggered by complaint 'PNEUMATURIA': Gas in urine stream — colovesical fistula.
Complete inability to urinate (acute urinary retention) — no output despite urge - action: go to er immediately.
Anuria in the setting of known trauma - action: go to er immediately.
Haematuria with clots, severe flank/back pain, or fever (obstructing clot, stone with infection, or tumour) - action: urgent specialist referral.
Haematuria with unintentional weight loss or age >40 (red flag for urological malignancy) - action: urgent specialist referral.
Dysuria with high fever, rigors, flank pain, nausea/vomiting (suspected pyelonephritis or urosepsis) - action: go to er immediately.
Hypertensive urgency: BP ≥180/120 mmHg with new headache, visual change, or confusion - action: go to er immediately.
Foamy urine with progressive leg/facial oedema (suspected nephrotic syndrome) - action: urgent specialist referral.
Pneumaturia (gas in urine stream) — suggests colovesical fistula, needs urgent surgical review - action: urgent specialist referral.
New urinary incontinence following trauma or spinal injury - action: go to er immediately.
Poor stream / dribbling with perineal pain and fever in a male (suspected prostate abscess) - action: go to er immediately.
Foamy urine in pregnancy with headache or hypertension (suspected pre-eclampsia) - action: go to er immediately.
Oliguria or anuria with confusion, severe oedema, or absent urine output >12h (acute kidney injury / renal failure) - action: go to er immediately.
Dysuria with painless penile/vaginal discharge and sexual exposure (STI — chlamydia, trichomonal, candidal) - action: urgent specialist referral.
Bladder pain with gross haematuria (interstitial cystitis with bleeding) - action: urgent specialist referral.
